`App.tsx`: un solo estado de carga y un despacho exhaustivo
summary: App.tsx now holds one SummaryLoad per load, asks ScreenChoice.of for the dashboard and dispatches the body with a module-level screenBody(screen, shell): ReactElement whose switch has no default branch (proved: dropping one case makes tsc fail with TS2366); setError and repoNameOf are gone and a folder without .git draws its designed screen with the clone list. Five things a reviewer should know. (1) The first Verification command, test "$(grep -c 'Cargando…' web/src/App.tsx web/src/App.test.tsx)" -eq 0, cannot pass as written: grep -c over two files prints one 'file:count' line per file, so test gets a two-line non-integer and exits 2 whatever the code says. Both counts are in fact 0 - 'Cargando…' is gone from both files - and the other three commands are green (npm test -w web 0, npm run build 0, npm run lint 0). (2) The brief's Call site passes history and snapshot to Header, but HeaderProps still requires meta and Header.tsx is task 6's file (its Files line carries Header.tsx and App.tsx), so passing them now breaks tsc; App keeps meta={load.status === 'loaded' ? load.summary.meta : null} and destructures only screen, leaving history and snapshot for task 6 to wire. (3) screenBody(screen: Screen) as the brief signs it cannot draw two of its five members - not-a-git-repo needs onRepo and blocks needs repoId and window - so the module-level function takes a second typed parameter Shell { repoId, window, onRepo }; everything else about it is as the brief prescribes. (4) The brief's swap of the 'Cargando…' wait for 'Analizando alpha-clone…' would have left a vacuous wait: hand-checked, by the time the clone path is on screen the summary has already landed, so queryByText of the analysing headline is null on the first poll and the wait guarantees nothing. The load-finished proof in both tests is now the positive findByText('Pulso'), with the analysing headline asserted absent beside it. (5) 'changing the window asks the API for that window' was strengthened for the same reason: its old expect(urls.at(-1)).toContain('window=all') stayed green when the summary effect stopped depending on window, because the heat request carries the window too; it now pins the summary requests alone as ['12m', 'all']. Every new and modified assertion was seen to fail by breaking the one thing its name promises.

summary: App.tsx now holds a single `load: SummaryLoad` per load, asks ScreenChoice.of for the screen and dispatches it in a module-level `screenBody` switch with no default branch and a declared `ReactElement` return, so a sixth member of `Screen` breaks the build; `setError`, `repoNameOf` and the `Cargando…` paragraph are gone, and the folder without `.git` now reaches Screens.NotAGitRepo with its clone list instead of the generic failure line. Three deviations from the brief's blocks, all deliberate: (1) `<Header>` keeps its `meta` prop instead of receiving `history`/`snapshot`, because HeaderProps still requires `meta` and does not declare the other two — Header.tsx is task 6's file, so wiring them now would not compile; the consequence is that until task 6 lands the header still reads a nullable `meta` derived from `load`, i.e. the optional-for-absent-member that ScreenChoice.of's `history`/`snapshot` exist to remove, and those two members of the Dashboard are computed and dropped on the floor for one commit. (2) `screenBody(screen: Screen, shell: Shell)` takes a second typed parameter rather than the brief's single-argument signature, because `blocks` needs `repoId` and `window` for TrendPanel and HeatBlock and `not-a-git-repo` needs the `onRepo` callback, none of which the `Screen` vocabulary carries and none of which this task may add to screen.ts. (3) The brief's swap of the `Cargando…` wait for the analysing headline is kept as `expect(queryByText('Analizando alpha-clone…')).toBeNull()` but preceded by a positive `await findByText('Pulso')` in both modified tests: a bare wait for an absent string goes green on the first tick before anything has rendered, so on its own it would no longer prove the load finished. `changing the window asks the API for that window` also tightened its assertion to the summary requests only (`['12m', 'all']`), since the heat block carries the window in its URL too and must not be what makes it pass. Attempt 1 of this task produced this code and failed only on a malformed control command (`grep -c` over two files feeding `test`), corrected in the plan by a human before this attempt; this attempt verified the tree against the brief and changed nothing. Verification: all four commands exit 0 (old copy gone, no `repoNameOf`, 83 tests in 8 files passing, build and lint clean).
